annotations.text:
Brownie v2 — the bets on top of the shipping app.

Click around the prototype: Loops in the sidebar, the Rohan card → brief, the Sunday letter, Recipes → Teach Hands (a 3-step flow), the footer link → What left your Mac, Settings → Brain → This Mac only, Settings → Privacy → Erase everything.

First-time tips play once per new screen and complete on the action, as in v1.

Knowledge as the product — four screens to react to.

1 · Ask: every claim carries a chip; clicking opens the original chat, mail or note.
2 · Notes: the knowledge base is an Obsidian vault — [[wikilinks]], Open in Obsidian, a mirror in iCloud Drive for the phone.
3 · Settings → Knowledge: vault location, Obsidian, iCloud; and “Let your other AIs read your notes” — Brownie as an MCP server that runs ON THIS MAC only (no hosting, no port, no account): Claude Desktop / Cursor / Raycast start it on demand. ChatGPT needs a public URL, so it's marked not possible. Per-app allow list and a log of what each app asked.
4 · Settings → Overnight: reads during the day every hour / 3 hours, only when idle and on power.

Six bets, designed before they're built — click through in the prototype too.

1–2 · Two-way vault sync: Settings → Knowledge gets Off / To the phone / Two-way, a last-sync line and the conflict rule (your words never overwritten; Brownie's version goes under its own heading). A note shows the line that came from the phone.
3 · Ask from anywhere: ⌘⇧Space over any app; a question is answered inline with citation chips; anything else is a Hands goal or a recipe.
4–5 · Due-aware nudges: loops with dates show when the card will come (Mon 7:30); a card appears the morning before even if nothing new was said; setting: morning before / 2 days / only when asked.
6–7 · Voice Memos and meeting audio, transcribed on the GPU at night; a promise said out loud becomes a loop with a 12-second clip as evidence. Slack with channel picking; Teams via Microsoft sign-in.
8 · Recipes on a trigger: When a file arrives in a folder matching a pattern; the file is a parameter; it still waits for you at the last step.

A household — Brownie for two people who share a life, without sharing a Mac or their private chats.

How it works: each person keeps their own Brownie and their own vault. A household is one shared iCloud Drive folder both Macs sync to. Only group chats BOTH people are in can be shared (Brownie checks the member list); direct messages, mail, files and People/ notes never cross over.

1 · Settings → Household: who you share with, which of the eligible chats, and the plain list of what never leaves.
2 · For You gets an “Ours” band: each card says who’s on it (you / Priya / either), and a card the other person already handled shows up dimmed with “Priya did this” — so you don’t both reply to the school.
3 · Loops gets an Ours section with an owner column. Either Brownie can close a loop; the other sees it the next sync.
4 · Household/ notes are written by both Macs; a line that came from a chat only the other person has is marked with their Mac.

Open questions for you: should the partner be able to see your CARD text for shared items (it is derived only from shared chats, so I think yes)? And do you want a third slot (a nanny, a flatmate) or is two the product?
